title: Publishable metadata and a clean package
summary: Add the identity metadata crates.io requires, exclude local secrets, and use cargo package to inspect the result.

scenario.briefing: The campus CLI has no description or license, and its package would include a local .env file. Add publishable metadata, exclude local secrets, and prepare a dry run.

objectives.description: Declare publish metadata and package exclusions.
Explain what cargo package includes and publishes.
Resolve a path-only dependency before publishing.

hints: crates.io requires a description and a license expression.
Add repository, keywords, and categories for discoverability.
exclude keeps local files out of the packaged archive.
Use cargo package --list and cargo publish --dry-run before publishing.

misconceptions.description: Publishing without a description or license.
misconceptions.feedback: crates.io rejects a package without the required identity fields. Add description and license at minimum.

misconceptions.description: Shipping local secrets in the package archive.
misconceptions.feedback: The package includes files by default. Use exclude to keep .env and private fixtures out of the archive.

misconceptions.description: Publishing a dependency with a wildcard requirement.
misconceptions.feedback: A wildcard lets every future resolve pick a different release. Publish a real version requirement.

misconceptions.description: Believing target/ is included in the crate archive.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Selecting the statement that target/ is published with the crate.
misconceptions.feedback: Cargo excludes target/ and VCS metadata by default. The manifest still controls other local files.

misconceptions.description: Publishing a path dependency without a version.
misconceptions.feedback: A path is local to the workspace. crates.io consumers need a version requirement next to the path.

sections.title: Publishing is a manifest contract
sections.body: crates.io requires a name, version, description, and license. repository, keywords, and categories help consumers find the crate. The license field uses an SPDX expression such as MIT OR Apache-2.0.

sections.title: The package is a file subset
sections.body: cargo package builds the archive that cargo publish uploads. Cargo excludes target/ and VCS internals by default, but it does not know which project files are secret. include and exclude decide what else enters the archive.

sections.title: Paths are local; versions are portable
sections.body: A path dependency works inside the workspace because the directory exists. A crates.io consumer resolves from the registry, so the dependency also needs a version requirement. workspace.dependencies can carry the shared version.

vocabulary.definition: A standardized license identifier, optionally combined with AND or OR.

steps.title: Make the manifest publishable
steps.prompt: Edit Cargo.toml. Add a description, an SPDX license, a repository, keywords, and categories, and exclude local secrets from the package.
hints: Keep the name, version, and edition.
Add keywords and categories as arrays.
Use exclude for .env and private fixtures.

localVerification.description: Verify the manifest still builds and tests the crate.

steps.title: What the package contains
hints: Separate what Cargo excludes by default from what the manifest adds.
dev-dependencies are for tests and examples.
A dry run exercises packaging and verification.

statements.label: crates.io requires a description and a license expression.
exclude removes matching paths from the package archive.
A published path dependency also needs a version requirement.
target/ is included in the published crate by default.
dev-dependencies are installed by consumers of the published crate.

steps.explanation: The manifest must identify the crate and its license. exclude controls extra local files, and path dependencies need versions for registry consumers. target/ and dev-dependencies are not part of a consumer's normal build.

steps.title: Transfer to a workspace publish
steps.prompt: A workspace member depends on another member with only path = "../core". What must be added before publishing?
hints: The registry does not know the local directory layout.
A version requirement lets Cargo resolve from crates.io.
Keep the path for local development and add the version.

quiz.prompt: A workspace member depends on another member with only path = "../core". What must be added before publishing?

options.label: A version requirement next to the path so registry consumers can resolve it.
Nothing; the path is uploaded and recreated on the consumer's machine.
Remove the dependency entirely because published crates cannot depend on each other.
Move the dependency to dev-dependencies so it is not published.

quiz.explanation: The path keeps the local workspace working, and the version tells crates.io how to resolve the dependency for consumers. Both belong on the dependency entry.

accessibility.summary: The workspace is keyboard accessible. Checks verify source structure and the reference tests; they do not compile or run the framework.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Use Tab to move between the editor and results. Ctrl+Enter runs the checks.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: Each check announces its description, whether it passed, and the missing or forbidden source fragment or test failure.
